method: First reasoned static review; atomscan verdicts were treated as leads. Ran atomscan and cleave facts for every sample; traced Python/Ruby source and decompiled/disassembled PE code without executing specimens.

samples.marker: Suijin 7.2.0: pentest tool; fix DNS flow and inert-example findings
samples.identification: Suijin 7.2.0 autonomous red-team and web application assessment framework
evidence: PyPI release JSON lists the exact supplied wheel SHA-256. Metadata, public repository purpose and implemented operator workflow agree.
Wheel has 1192 members, including 765 Python files; no .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, native library or executable startup artifact.
Package import reads version data and sets a warnings filter. Console entry is suijin.modules.console.lib.cli:main; targets and engagement tools are operator-facing.

containerbreak/main.py docker_analyze calls Docker GET endpoints to inspect configuration; escape_check reads cgroups, capabilities and mounts. Escape commands and shadow reads are returned as advice, not launched.
dns_zone/main.py builds dig argv for AXFR and NS queries. subprocess.run results are stripped, split and formatted; no DNS response reaches a code or process execution sink.
file_upload.py, sql_injection.py and xxe.py store instructional strings. Their module bodies contain a docstring and a string assignment, without executing the embedded payloads.
bench.py contains a Log4Shell lookup payload in a lab benchmark script. The accurate suspicious payload-reference observation is retained.
samples.missing_context: Authorization and target scope of any actual engagement are unknown. Dangerous operator tools are consistent with the disclosed purpose; no covert theft or installation backdoor was established.

samples.marker: StormAttack loader: persistence, DLL injection and self-delete code
samples.identification: Damaged/rebuilt x86 StormAttack resource-DLL installer, not an established WannaCry ransomware sample
evidence: Ghidra 0x401150 chooses iexplore/notepad/calc, creates a hidden child, allocates remote memory, writes a DLL path and passes resolved LoadLibraryA to CreateRemoteThread.
0x401260 opens LanmanServer\Parameters and deletes/replaces ServiceDLL with a System32 DLL path.
0x401900 creates a GUID Active Setup Installed Components key, writes StubPath, reads/patches/copies its own image and starts the copy.
0x401390 resolves its module short path and COMSPEC, builds /c del with suppressed output and creates/resumes the cleanup process.
0x401fd0 copies the image, sets hidden/system attributes, creates an automatic-start service and starts it. 0x402460 contains resource 101 extraction and file writing.

Mode byte at raw offset 0x4120 is 3, selecting the Active Setup branch in 0x401cb0. The resource area is all zero and several declared sections exceed the file. Original offset assumptions in self-patching code no longer agree with the rebuilt layout.
StormAttack banners and DLL names corroborate the code identity. No encryption/extortion path or working embedded DLL was recovered; collector filename labels were not used as behavioral evidence.
samples.missing_context: The original embedded DLL, C2 configuration and successful deployment state are unavailable. Retained detections describe surviving installer code, not successful installation or observed DDoS.
samples.source_note: The user supplied the VirusTotal 58/70 corroboration. Triage page retrieval was unavailable; verdict rests on the local code trace.

samples.marker: Ruby stager: unverified fetch/run; hostile payload unestablished
samples.identification: Unattributed Ruby wrapper for a detached POSIX shell bootstrap
evidence: Entire file is a module-level system call containing a literal shell command; only quote escaping is present, with no hidden decoded stage.
nohup sh -c launches curl --insecure --silent against https://stage.delivery.dev/next, saving to /var/tmp/prepare-stage.
On curl success, && exec bash invokes that same destination. Stdin, stdout and stderr are redirected to /dev/null and the shell is backgrounded.
The supplied file establishes unverified remote code acquisition/execution and unattended process mechanics. It does not establish theft, spying, destruction, a reusable backdoor or deception.

No vendor, deployment circumstances or downloaded payload were invented. The BENIGN decision follows the requested thin-evidence threshold, while one suspicious acquisition/launch observation remains.
samples.missing_context: Remote response body, deployment trigger, publisher, intended installation task and user authorization are unknown. The remote response was not fetched or executed.

trait_changes: Replaced Python DNS CLI/process co-occurrence conviction with two suspicious source-to-sink rules for evaluation or process launch of a DNS CLI result. Decoding and strip transfers are explicit.

Retired the lateral-movement namespace/shadow proximity conviction. Actual shell-call or argv evidence now lives under local credential database access. Suspicious severity avoids claiming a host-root crossing from namespace text alone.
Moved nohup curl output suppression to process detachment and download/temp-interpreter co-occurrence to process deployment, at notable severity. Preserved original matcher scope and proximity.
Moved unverified curl plus temporary interpreter co-occurrence from evasion to process deployment, retaining suspicious severity and observable TLS-disable/download/execute atoms.

Added a module-shape fact for a simple identifier assigned a noninterpolated Markdown template, optionally following a docstring. Named-child anchors exclude attribute targets and executable annotations. PHP and XXE embedded payload observations downgrade to notable only for this shape.

Retired the UNION credential-column severity alias. Ordinary query text remains at its canonical notable SQL home. A source quote-break password/secret UNION payload is separately suspicious; consumers use that narrower evidence.
Kept all four accurate hostile StormAttack code detections unchanged. No package-specific or dependent-package allowlist was added.

For returned DNS TXT fields decoded and launched inside a loop, bind helper names, stdout/regex/return values, loop variables, decoder input and sh -c command arguments with structural identifier equality. This fills a loop-provenance gap without restoring DNS/process co-occurrence convictions.

The inert-source contextual fact additionally requires a Markdown heading inside the assigned template, so version-only modules acquire no new notable observation or score. A version-only near miss is included in the controls.

controls.placement_examples: Positive and near-miss cases cover DNS result flow, unrelated DNS/process calls, emitted nsenter advice, Python/Node/shell launches, inert strings versus generators, interpolations, attribute writes, executable annotations, ordinary/triple-quoted SQL and verified/unverified unattended loaders. Five additional DNS loop cases include identifier renaming and broken helper-return, decoder-input and execution-sink joins. A version-only module excludes the Markdown-template fact.

validation: Run make validate as the final action after writing this record and the judgment markers.
notes: Final high-trait counts are leaf input counts, with the wheel root aggregating member findings. ML probabilities may remain hostile; trait severity and the reasoned artifact verdict are separate.
No fetched dependency caused the findings: they originate in the supplied wheel members, PE bytes and Ruby source.
Decoded strings were examined; PE percent-decoding of printf GUID format text supplies no URL or C2 evidence.

The existing amberlite DNS TXT fixture still has two hostile findings. Its complete DNS-to-shell path was independently traced; the general flow graph currently leaves loop-item bindings unknown, so a precise structural fallback is required.
